subtype: Lives for fun and good times [Actor]
passage: In Mahima's kasba, everyone knew when she was coming: loud laugh, bicycle bell, a bag of roasted peanuts to share. This week her whole calendar was the temple fair, the new film at the town's old cinema hall, and Friday's chaat trip with six friends. Her friends adored her; she made every plan feel like a festival. On Thursday, Bhavna stopped her at the school gate. "Mahi, the science project. It's due Monday. Have you started?" Mahima's smile faded. She hadn't even opened the book. She thought of the chaat trip, then of Sir's face on Monday. "Friday I'll go for one hour only," she said slowly. "And Saturday you come to my house and we do the project." Bhavna laughed. "One hour? You?"

qa.q: What was due on Monday?
qa.a: The science project.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling when her smile faded?
qa.a: She felt a jolt of worry and guilt, realising her fun plans had crowded out the project she hadn't started.

qa.q: What choice did Mahima make, and could it work?
qa.a: She cut the chaat trip to one hour and planned a work session with Bhavna on Saturday, which could keep some fun while getting the project done.

qa.q: How does Bhavna see Mahima's love of fun?
qa.a: Bhavna enjoys Mahima's energy but knows it can take over, which is why Bhavna reminds her and laughs at the 'one hour' promise.

grounding: A small-town teenager plans her week around fun and friends, which makes her loved but crowds out her schoolwork.

subtype: Lives for fun and good times [Actor]
passage: Sofia's weekend in Mexico City was full before it started: Saturday skating with the group, a street-taco crawl, the outdoor film in the park at night, and Sunday brunch at Layla's. Her phone buzzed with plans and heart emojis; everyone wanted Sofia there because she made things fun. The history essay due Monday sat in a tab she kept not clicking. On Sunday night, full and happy, she opened it. Blank. Her stomach sank. She messaged Layla: "Best weekend ever. Worst essay ever. 😬" Layla replied: "Library tomorrow at seven? I'll bring pan dulce." Sofia wrote the first paragraph, then another, telling herself next weekend would start with the boring part.

qa.q: What did Sofia keep not clicking?
qa.a: The tab with the history essay due Monday.

qa.q: What was Sofia feeling when she opened the blank essay?
qa.a: She felt her stomach sink, a mix of worry and regret after such a happy, busy weekend.

qa.q: What choice did Sofia make at the end, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: She started writing that night and decided future weekends would begin with the boring part, so fun no longer crowds out her work.

qa.q: How does Layla see Sofia?
qa.a: Layla clearly enjoys Sofia's company and wants to help, offering to meet at the library with pan dulce instead of judging her 😊

grounding: A teenager fills her weekend with outings and food, bringing joy and friends, but her essay suffers.

subtype: Lives for fun and good times [Actor]
passage: Asif was the reason Block C in the boarding school had movie nights. He booked the common room, smuggled in popcorn, and did voices for every villain. The juniors adored him. His roommate Karthik liked the fun too, but he also saw the stack of unfinished lab records on Asif's desk. When the mid-term results went up on the notice board, Asif's chemistry mark had dropped from seventy-eight to forty-one. He stood there a long time, then laughed too loudly. That night he didn't book the common room. Karthik found him at his desk under the lamp, copying equations. "Movie Saturday?" Karthik asked. Asif shrugged. "After I finish these. Maybe."

qa.q: What did Asif's chemistry mark drop to?
qa.a: It dropped from seventy-eight to forty-one.

qa.q: What does Asif laughing too loudly at the notice board suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt embarrassed and shaken by the drop, and was hiding it behind his usual fun.

qa.q: What was Asif's turning point, and what did he choose?
qa.a: Seeing the results, he chose not to book the common room and worked on his lab records, putting the work before the fun for a while.

qa.q: How does Karthik see Asif's fun-loving side?
qa.a: Karthik enjoys it but had noticed the unfinished records, so he sees both the joy Asif brings and the cost it had on his studies.

grounding: A boarding-school teenager lives for movie nights and fun, loved by friends, until his marks drop because fun crowded out work.

subtype: Lives for fun and good times [Actor]
passage:
Dear Uday,
Summer update from your favourite cousin! We made a list and did ALL of it: the new food lane near the station (the paneer rolls!), three films in one week, the late-night kulfi walk, and Mitali's birthday at the lake. I made two new friends from the kulfi walk alone. Mummy says her daughter lights up the house when I'm in a good mood, which is always, so.
Okay, confession. Our science project was due on Monday. I knew for a month. Every time I sat down it felt so boring compared to everything else. I finished it on Sunday night, badly. Ma'am wrote, "You are capable of more, Pallavi." That stung a bit, I won't lie.
I don't want to stop having fun. It's the best part of me. But maybe fun can't be the only thing on the list.
Write back and tell me about hostel food. Is it as bad as you said?
Pallavi

qa.q: What did Ma'am write on Pallavi's project?
qa.a: You are capable of more, Pallavi.

qa.q: How did Pallavi feel when she read Ma'am's comment?
qa.a: It stung; she felt a bit ashamed because she knew she had left the project till Sunday night even though she had a month.

qa.q: What choice is Pallavi starting to make after the project, and why?
qa.a: She wants to keep having fun but add duties to the list too, because she sees that letting fun rule everything left her work poor.

qa.q: How might Uday see Pallavi after reading this letter?
qa.a: Uday would likely see Pallavi as warm and full of life, the fun one, while noticing she is starting to think about balance.

grounding: It shows a teenager who plans her summer around food, films and outings, gains friends and energy from it, and sees fun crowd out her project.

subtype: Lives for fun and good times [Actor]
passage:
"Okay, so for the school magazine, you want to know why I'm 'the fun one'? I'm Yamini, Class 12, and honestly I've always been like this.
I plan everything. The class picnic to the waterfall? Me. Movie Fridays at my house? Me. When Ramesh's grandfather passed away, I organised a samosa evening for his family and just sat with him. Fun isn't only laughing. It's being together.
But here's the real story. In Class 11, I was so busy planning that I forgot to study for chemistry. I failed the half-yearly. Ramesh, my study partner, stopped calling me for group study because I always cancelled.
That hurt. So now I plan the fun and I plan the boring stuff too. Tuesday and Thursday evenings are for chemistry, no exceptions. Ramesh says I'm still the fun girl, just the fun girl who passes."

qa.q: What did Yamini organise for Ramesh's family?
qa.a: A samosa evening, and she sat with him.

qa.q: How did Yamini feel when Ramesh stopped calling her for group study?
qa.a: It hurt; she felt left out and realised her cancelling had pushed her study partner away.

qa.q: What was the turning point for Yamini, and what did she change?
qa.a: Failing the chemistry half-yearly and losing Ramesh's study calls made her start planning the boring work too, with fixed chemistry evenings.

qa.q: How does Ramesh seem to see Yamini now?
qa.a: He still sees her as the fun one who brings people together, but one who now keeps her study commitments.

grounding: It shows a teenager whose love of outings and fun brings energy and friends, until it crowds out her studies and she starts to balance it.
